title: feat(theme): palette inspired by Salesforce / SLDS
body: ## Summary Re-themes Cascade Goods using CSS custom properties in `src/index.css` only. The palette is **inspired by Salesforce / SLDS** (Cloud Blue `#00A1E0`, deep brand blue `#032D60`, cool neutrals). This is a visual demo change and does not imply official Salesforce affiliation. Also fixes `CheckoutSuccessPage` so the order is read from `sessionStorage` in a `useState` lazy initializer instead of `useEffect`, resolving an ESLint `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` error that blocked `npm run lint`. ## Token checklist (pairings reviewed for WCAG AA) | Token | Value | Paired / notes | |--------|--------|------------------| | `--color-brand` | `#032d60` | `--color-brand-foreground` `#ffffff` | | `--color-accent` | `#00a1e0` | `--color-accent-foreground` `#032d60` (navy on Cloud Blue for AA button text) | | `--color-foreground` | `#032d60` | on `--color-background` `#f3f2f2` | | `--color-muted-foreground` | `#5c6c7c` | on `--color-background` and `--color-muted` `#ecebea` | | `--color-card` / `--color-card-foreground` | `#ffffff` / `#032d60` | | | `--color-ring` | `#00a1e0` | focus vs page/card surfaces | | `--color-success` | `#2e844a` | on light backgrounds / badges | | `--color-destructive` | `#c23934` | `--color-destructive-foreground` `#ffffff` | Contrast checks: manual review against WCAG 2.1 AA targets (4.5:1 normal text); accent foreground explicitly chosen because white on `#00a1e0` fails AA for small UI text. ## Artifacts **Before** ![Cascade Goods home before theme](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-31ef1cfc-27de-4083-bcc2-098771eaf267) **After** ![Cascade Goods home after Salesforce-inspired theme](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-6622f43a-c99f-47f7-b822-a8c33127d79c) Screen recordings: home → Shop All (products) → Ridgeline Shell Jacket detail, ~3s per view. ## Verification - `npm run lint` - `npm run build` ## Rollback Revert `src/index.css` (and optionally `CheckoutSuccessPage.tsx` if only theme is reverted) or revert the merge commit.
